scope: Plain-language descriptions; rate authority is qualified where local instruments remain unverified. Budget labels identify accounts, not every underlying transaction.

311.100.text: Property owners pay this tax on taxable property value; the city receives its share through the tax collector. The Commission sets the city millage through the annual budget process, subject to state limits and voting requirements.

311.200.text: These are overdue property-tax payments from earlier tax years. The city cannot increase past bills by changing today’s millage; collections depend on outstanding taxes and the statutory collection process.

millage.text: Millage is the city’s property-tax rate, not a revenue amount: one mill is $1 per $1,000 of taxable value. The Commission adopts the rate through public budget hearings, subject to state limits and voting requirements.

312.410.text: Fuel buyers fund this county-imposed local-option fuel tax, and Panama City receives an allocated share. The city cannot change the county’s rate by itself; county action and the distribution agreement or state formula govern it.

314.100.text: Customers pay this city public-service tax on taxable electricity purchases, and the seller remits it. The city may change its levy by ordinance within state limits; the general statutory ceiling is 10%, but this card does not establish unused capacity under the current local rate.

315.100.text: Customers pay communications-services tax on taxable services such as phone and television service; providers remit it for distribution.
